text:
maria: Quick sync — we hit a design snag in the authn/authz plane. How should TTL inheritance work when a service token is proxied to downstream routes that issue derived tokens? Current options: inherit parent's TTL (clamped to route max), always issue fresh fixed TTL, or require explicit route opt-in. Thoughts?

jon: my vote: inherit but clamp to route_max. keeps least surprise and avoids longer-lived derived creds than parent. add a small safety jitter. :+1:

lee: prefer explicit opt-in via route config. implicit inheritance makes audit reasoning harder. defaults: inherit_clamped but make routes opt-out to fresh issuance.

anita: important: rotation/refresh pattern. if child inherits, refresh semantics on parent expiry get tricky. we need clear rules for who can refresh child tokens and when. also telemetry for token lineage (parent_id -> child_ids).

samir: two practical gotchas: 1) role projection per-route can widen privileges if we don't constrain TTL. 2) long parent TTL + short route_max -> silent truncation could break long-running jobs. need failure-mode policy: reject issuance if parent_ttl > route_max unless route allows truncate.

security-bot: note: audit rule suggestion: log derived_token { parent_id, parent_ttl, issued_ttl, route, actor } on every issue.

maria: agreed on logging. proposal below (pseudo-yaml):

    route_auth:
      inherit_ttl: true
      max_ttl: 1h
      ttl_mode: clamp_to_parent # options: clamp_to_parent | fresh | require_opt_in

lee: minor nit: use explicit enum values and document migration. also add field: ttl_truncate_behavior: reject | truncate | warn. default warn is noisy.

jon: +1 for truncate_behavior. I think default should be reject for first rollout, to surface breakages. then switch to truncate after opt-in.

anita: about RBAC projection: if route strips roles or maps to narrower roles, inheriting TTL is ok. but if route enlarges role set we must forbid inheritance (or force manual approve). we need a check: if projected_roles ⊄ parent_roles then issuance should fail unless route_override_flag is set.

samir: for per-request actor affinity we can require X-Actor-ID header propagated from caller and assert it in derived token. sample:

    curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer PARENT\" -H \"X-Actor-ID: user:alice\" https://proxy/route

sre-bot: deployment note: adding TTL inheritance will touch token cache behavior. we should add a cache-key variant that includes parent_id + route + ttl_mode to avoid cache pollution.

maria: migration plan suggestion:
- phase 1 (opt-in): implement clamp_to_parent + reject on role-expansion; routes must opt-in via inherit_ttl: true
- phase 2 (default change): after 2 weeks of metrics and low rejection rate, change default to inherit_clamped + truncate_behavior: truncate with audit warning
- phase 3 (full rollout): allow routes to request fresh issuance and override behavior via admin review

anita: add telemetry gating: token_churn, rejection_rate(role_expansion), average_derived_ttl, lineage_depth. expose per-route dashboards.

jon: open question: should parent token with infinite/very-long TTL be treated specially? i.e., cap at org_default_max (e.g., 24h) regardless of parent. otherwise a long-lived parent could keep derived creds alive forever.

maria: yes, enforce org_default_max. we should also document that operator tokens (platform-level) cannot be proxied to produce derived tokens unless explicit allowlist.

samir: edge-case: background workers that intentionally need >1h derived creds. offer a signed request flow: route can request a time-limited extension with admin approval; track it in audit.

security-bot: flagged: need CL around KMS key usage for derived tokens, and TTL enforcement in the token verifier (not just issuer).

maria: ACTIONS:
- jon: sketch RFC with the three modes and migration plan (due EOD Fri)
- lee + anita: list routes that must opt-out or need special handling (by Tue)
- infra: add cache-key change ticket and telemetry fields (sre-bot will create)

jon: will do. will include sample audit log schema.

lee: thanks — i'll run a quick route-audit to find role-expansion candidates.

maria: great. linking RFC draft here when ready. thanks everyone. :rocket:
